newsitem.title: UK: IEA revises down projections for non-OPEC supply.
newsitem.headline: IEA revises down projections for non-OPEC supply.

text.p: Oil supplies from non-OPEC producers will not hit the heights previously expected at the end of this year, leaving extra room for OPEC crude on world markets, the International Energy Agency said on Friday.
The Paris-based agency, in its monthly Oil Market Report, revised down its projections for non-OPEC supplies for both the third and fourth quarters of the year by 300,000 barrels per day (bpd).
"Primarily as a result of decreases in projections of non-OPEC supplies, the call on OPEC crude plus stock changes has been increased," the IEA said.
The IEA's third quarter call-on-OPEC oil projection was increased by 300,000 bpd to 24.2 million bpd and the fourth quarter estimate by 400,000 bpd to 25.6 million.
The agency said it still expected world oil demand to rise sharply again next year with increased demand among developing nations making up for slower growth from industrialised OECD countries.

"While OECD demand growth is expected to slow in 1997, primarily due to an assumed return to normal weather, non-OECD growth is forecast to accelerate, mainly due to an assumed slowdown in the decline in FSU (former Soviet Union) demand."
Main demand estimates were left unchanged from last month's IEA report.
World demand was expected to rise by 1.8 million barrels per day (bpd) to 73.6 million in 1997, up 2.5 percent on top of this year's 1.7 million bpd growth to 71.8 million, the IEA said.
